properties.name: The 117 unattributed gap acknowledgements were backfilled to who:ajs
properties.rationale:
⚠️ THESE 117 EDGES DELIBERATELY CARRY NO `acted_at`, AND A LATER SESSION MUST NOT READ THAT AS AN OVERSIGHT. Stamping them 2026-08-29 would assert that Anthony judged 117 gaps in one morning, which is false; the real judgement dates are spread over 2026-07-23..2026-08-28 and were never recorded per-acknowledgement, so null is the only true value. Absent means "not recorded", and that is the honest answer.

THE SECOND REASON MATTERS MORE, because it protects a measurement. #368's root-cause analysis turned on dates: all 51 pre-existing approver edges on the gap side are dated 2026-08-23/24, the day `acknowledge_gap` shipped its `approver` parameter, and THAT CLUSTERING IS WHAT REFUTED the comfortable reading that 30% attribution meant careless callers. It established that the parameter gets used when it exists, which is what made its ABSENCE on `acknowledge_defect` the cause rather than caller behaviour. Backdating or same-dating this backfill would drop 117 synthetic points into exactly that distribution and destroy the evidence — a future session re-running the analysis would see 168 attributed acknowledgements clustered on two days and conclude something that was never true.

So the record of the backfill lives HERE, in one event that says what happened and when, rather than in 117 timestamps that would each say something slightly false.

This closes the caller-side half of `cap:an-acknowledgement-says-whose-judgement-it-was` for the gap family: the parameter shipped 2026-08-23, the sibling tool was fixed in #368, and this is the history the parameter could not have carried because it did not exist yet.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary: Every `decision:ack:*` gap acknowledgement that carried no approver — 117 of the 168 — was given an AUTHORED_BY role=approver edge to who:ajs, on Anthony's explicit word this session ("for the 117 unattributed acknowledgements, you can attribute them to me"). Written as one atomic create_edges call. Nothing about the acknowledgements themselves changed; only the record of whose judgement they were, which is why this is on the `record` axis. The set was verified against the committed export before writing: 117 is exactly the residue #368 measured, and no rationale in it attributes the judgement to anyone else. Four mention another name (Alex, the storyflow fleet) and all four are incidental — the trials programme lists storyflow among the real designs reflow2 is used on, and the Alex one is who:ajs's own standing policy re-firing because a capability joined the affected set. Thirty-one name no person at all; every one of those is an agent re-application of a standing disposition Anthony set (the trials-programme policy of 2026-07-23, dec:intent-preserved's post-cut rule), so the approver is his even though the prose does not say a name. The 9 unattributed `acknowledge_defect` acknowledgements are NOT in this set and remain unattributed.
